chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said:

When the maghrib salat (prayer) is performed in a state of fear, he divides them into two groups. He leads one group in two rakʿahs, then he sits with them. Then he signals to them with his hand, and each person among them stands and performs one rakʿah, then they give salām and go to the place of their companions. Then the other group comes; they say the takbīr and enter into the salat (prayer). The Imam stands and leads them in one rakʿah, then gives salām. Then each man among them stands and performs one rakʿah, joining it to the one he performed with the Imam, then he stands and performs one rakʿah in which there is no recitation. Thus the Imam completes three rakʿahs, the first group has two rakʿahs in congregation, and the latter ones individually. So the first ones have the takbīr and opening of the salat (prayer), and the latter ones have the salām.

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: the opening declaration of Allah's greatness beginning the salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader who organizes and leads the salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْخَوْفِ: a state of fear or danger, especially in circumstances of conflict
key_terms.جَمَاعَةٍ: congregation, meaning prayer performed behind the Imam
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib salat (prayer), the evening obligatory prayer
key_terms.فِرْقَتَيْنِ: two groups into which the worshippers are divided

ai.seo_question: How is maghrib salat al-khawf performed according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of performing salat al-khawf for maghrib prayer by dividing the worshippers into two groups and alternating their participation behind the Imam. It details how the Imam and each group complete their rakʿahs so that prayer is maintained even in conditions of danger.
